newsitem.title: NEPAL: Bank of Ceylon unit to buy stake in Nepal Bank.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Ceylon unit to buy stake in Nepal Bank.

text.p: The Nepal Bank of Ceylon Ltd, a unit of Sri Lanka's Bank of Ceylon, will buy a five percent stake in a leading Nepali bank for 84.64 million Nepali rupees ($1.48 million), government officials said on Tuesday.
They said the Nepal Bank of Ceylon would pay 1,131 Nepali rupees per share for 74,837 shares of Nepal Bank Ltd.

"The Nepal Bank of Ceylon Ltd was the highest of two bidders for five percent of shares offered by the government for block purchase," Narendra Man Shrestha, an official at the Nepali Finance Ministry's privatisation division, told Reuters.
He said the government wanted to gradually reduce its stakes in the Nepal Bank Ltd, the largest financial institution in the Himalayan kingdom.

The government currently holds 46 percent of the Nepal Bank's equity while the public owns the rest. Last year the government sold five percent of the bank's shares to its employees as part of a privatisation policy, officials said.
A Finance Ministry statement said an agreement for the deal had already been signed with the buyer.

The state-owned Bank of Ceylon holds a 45 percent stake in Nepal Bank of Ceylon Ltd. Nepali investors hold 25 percent of the bank's equity while the remaining 30 percent is due to be publicly floated later this year.
